clue.text: Screen star's apartments?

parts.note: the sun is our nearest star; the possessive adds no letter
a block of flats holds many apartments

explanation.surface: A question about where a film star lives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Screen' looks like cinema beside 'star', but it is a protective cream.
explanation.definitionFit: A cream that blocks ultraviolet light is a screen against the sun's rays.

clue.text: Heel tilts toe out of place

indicators.note: letters put out of place are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A shoe heel that tips the toe awkwardly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of place' rearranges TILTS and TOE.
explanation.definitionFit: A stiletto is a tall thin heel on a woman's shoe, named after the dagger.

clue.text: Yield for Mussolini?

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for
Mussolini styled himself Il Duce, the leader

explanation.surface: Asking what output the Italian dictator might want.
explanation.walkthrough: Mussolini's title was Il Duce, 'the leader'.
explanation.definitionFit: Farm produce is the yield of the land, crops and goods grown.

clue.text: Overhaul salesman's appearance

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative; the possessive adds no letter
an air is a manner or appearance

explanation.surface: Smartening up a travelling salesman's looks.
explanation.definitionFit: To repair something is to overhaul and fix it, verb for verb.

clue.text: Large number taken in by tale, getting wild

indicators.note: something taken in by another is held inside it

parts.note: a story is a tale
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, a large number

explanation.surface: A story that grows huge and gets out of hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Stormy weather or a stormy temper is wild and turbulent.

clue.text: Forger seen in bar, assembling it free

parts.note: a counter is the bar where drinks are served

indicators.note: assembling puts the parts together in a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A forger caught in a pub, putting together a plan to get away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assembling' rearranges IT and FREE into FEITER.
explanation.definitionFit: A counterfeiter makes fake money or goods, a forger by trade.

clue.text: Mistake in the parish records?

parts.note: a slip in office paperwork, pictured as one made by the vicar who keeps the parish registers

explanation.definitionFit: A clerical error is an office slip; clerical also means of the clergy.

clue.text: Eccentrically beg her fortune for luck

indicators.note: something done eccentrically is done oddly, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Pleading with a fortune teller for good luck.
explanation.definitionFit: The rub of the green is a golfing idiom for chance or luck that goes for or against you.

clue.text: The lady's sphere mostly is found in aromatic plants

parts.note: her is the possessive for a lady

indicators.note: mostly means all but the final letter of the word

parts.note: a ball is a sphere

explanation.surface: A woman's world is found among fragrant plants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts the last L from BALL.
explanation.definitionFit: Herbal describes what comes from herbs, which are aromatic plants.

clue.text: Getting back, help clan in onslaught

indicators.note: getting back means the word is turned round to read backwards

parts.note: aid is help
a tribe is a clan

explanation.surface: Coming back to aid one's family in an attack.
explanation.definitionFit: A diatribe is a bitter verbal attack, an onslaught of words.

clue.text: Member in European Union being unable to take flight

indicators.note: in places the member's letter inside the union's letters

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for member, as in MP or MEP

explanation.surface: An MEP grounded in Brussels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being' makes the definition a creature, not a state.
explanation.definitionFit: The emu is a large Australian bird that cannot fly.

clue.text: Two possibilities for batsman making attack

parts.note: in cricket a batsman may hit the ball, or be out; both outcomes are given
in cricket a batsman may hit the ball, or be out; both outcomes are given

explanation.surface: A cricket batsman with two options when going on the offensive.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the batsman either hits the ball or is dismissed, OUT.
explanation.definitionFit: To hit out is a phrasal verb meaning to attack, physically or in words.

clue.text: Win takeaway?

definitions.meaning: to ... a prize is to win it
to carry food off is to take it away, as with a takeaway meal

explanation.definitionFit: Carry off means both to win a prize and to remove something by taking it away.

clue.text: River, one with a drowned valley

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A river described as having a submerged valley.
explanation.definitionFit: A ria is a long narrow inlet formed when the sea floods a river valley.

clue.text: Sustain record arrears

parts.note: to back someone is to support or sustain them
a log is a written record

explanation.surface: Supporting a record of unpaid debts.
explanation.definitionFit: A backlog is a build-up of work or payments left outstanding, like arrears.

clue.text: Great number who fled wicked city

definitions.meaning: in Genesis the man who escaped Sodom before it was destroyed

explanation.definitionFit: Lot means a large amount, and is the biblical figure who fled Sodom.

clue.text: Restore your old well

parts.note: to heal is to restore to health
thy is the old form of your

explanation.surface: Bring back your old water well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'well' looks like a noun, a water well; it is the adjective meaning in good health.
explanation.definitionFit: Being well means being in good health, fit and sound.

clue.text: Remarkable sixth sense Alice misconstrued

parts.note: ESP, extrasensory perception, is called the sixth sense

indicators.note: a name misconstrued is taken the wrong way, so its letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Alice's sixth sense is misread.
explanation.definitionFit: Especial means exceptional or particularly notable, so remarkable.

clue.text: Seducer finding harlot dancing before ten

indicators.note: letters dancing move about into a new order

parts.note: IO looks like 10, ten in figures

explanation.surface: A womaniser spots a prostitute dancing before ten o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' rearranges HARLOT into LOTHAR; IO is 1 and 0, read as letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Lothario, a rake in an old play, became a byword for a womanising seducer.

clue.text: Type of film we back

parts.note: the stern is the back of a ship

explanation.surface: We go back to a film genre.
explanation.definitionFit: A western is a film genre about cowboys in the American West.

clue.text: Stored porridge maintained pulse

parts.note: kept means stored
porridge is British slang for a prison sentence, time served

explanation.surface: Porridge kept in the cupboard.
explanation.walkthrough: PORRIDGE is British slang for a jail term, as in the sitcom.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping time means maintaining a steady beat or rhythm, like a pulse.

clue.text: Nervous reaction suppresses part of play strategy

indicators.note: to suppress is to keep something held down within, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: a tic is a nervous twitch
an act is a division of a play

explanation.surface: Fighting down a twitch during part of a play is a plan.
explanation.definitionFit: A tactic is a planned move, a strategy for gaining an end.

clue.text: Strike camp — it disintegrates

indicators.note: something that disintegrates falls apart and its letters reform differently

explanation.surface: Breaking camp as it falls apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strike camp' reads as packing tents; 'Strike' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An impact is a collision or blow, a strike.

clue.text: Boy gets around to returning soup

indicators.note: gets around means one word wraps round another piece

parts.note: a page is a boy servant

indicators.note: returning means the little word is read backwards

explanation.surface: A lad comes back to some soup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' reverses the little word, and 'gets around' wraps the boy's synonym round the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Potage is a thick French-style soup.

clue.text: Little girl's confident but not right

indicators.note: not means the named letter is left out

parts.note: sure means confident

explanation.surface: A young girl who is self-assured but in the wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Sue is a short girl's name, a little girl in crossword shorthand.

clue.text: Idiot takes two different drugs

parts.note: crack is a form of cocaine and pot is cannabis
crack is a form of cocaine and pot is cannabis

explanation.surface: A fool on two kinds of drug.
explanation.definitionFit: A crackpot is an eccentric or foolish person.

clue.text: Swiss Cottage?

parts.note: a London district name read literally as a timber house in the Alps

explanation.definitionFit: A chalet is a wooden cottage typical of Switzerland; Swiss Cottage is a London district.

clue.text: New start in life requires restraint before growth

parts.note: a rein is a restraint
a carnation is a flower, something grown

explanation.surface: Starting life afresh needs self-control before personal growth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'growth' suggests development; here it is a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Reincarnation is rebirth of the soul in a new body, a new start in life.
